newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins track Brady rise, dip on Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins track Brady rise, dip on Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices firmed in early trading on Wednesday to follow a general upward trend in other markets, but edged down later on news that Boris Yeltsin would stay in hospital all week, dealers said.
Yeltsin's doctor Sergei Mironov said the president's pneumonia was a serious illness that could lead to complications. But he said Yeltsin's condition had stabilised over the last three days.
"MinFins followed the Bradies-upward trend in early trading, but then bounced slightly back after Yeltsin news," one dealer said.
"But the market is looking upwards and everybody is seeing higher levels after some previous days of decline."
A Mosbiznesbank dealer said MinFins had found support from Moscow-based buying, a phenomenon not seen much in 1996 when Westerners supported the market.
Dealers said the market would look to results of the International Monetary Fund's Russia mission, which began on Wednesday, and final approval of a 1997 federal budget.
The IMF mission is in Moscow monitoring Russia's economic performance in December and the first half of January.
Russia's lower parliament chamber is to hold its fourth and final reading of draft budget on January 24.
